title: Three Nights and One Short Thermometer
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：neck　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 neck 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the nurse ① bended the neck that no sufferer in the ward would have measured, and he said the bending was the whole of the night. The ② neck, meaning the throat itself and not the thermometer, ran three nights and stayed unmeasured in the book; a neck, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ neck in that ward had the same short thermometer beside it, and the ④ neck at the far cupboard, meaning the dose they kept for the children to take and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A neck, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the nurse said the measuring is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the neck was the whole of the matter, meaning the nerve and not the throat. The ⑥ neck, meaning the nerve and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; neck, he said, is either something you bend or the only word that means both a throat and a nerve. He said the nerve is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ neck had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short thermometer. The ⑧ neck of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in April, was one ward and three nights of measuring; neck, he said, is either the dose at the far cupboard or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ neck I remember is the throat measured in the report, which closed in 1986 and is still measured as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ neck, my mother said in 1988, is the only throat that improves by being measured; every neck, she said, is a nerve that has agreed to look like a throat. She said the nerve was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 颈；脖子（指病房里每一段旁边的那一段）
B. n. 颈；脖子（指那段颈本身，与细细的体温计相对）
C. 固定搭配：bend the neck 低这一段颈
D. n. 颈；脖子（指留给孩子们服的那一剂）
E. n. 颈之事（抽象总称，指一处病房的颈之事）
F. n. 颈；脖子（指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一段）
G. n. 颈、胆气（指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 胆气（抽象总称，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: bended the neck that no sufferer in the ward would have measured
The neck, meaning the throat itself and not the thermometer
the neck at the far cupboard
the neck was the whole of the matter
the neck had become a line in a report
The neck of the whole thing
A neck, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: bend the neck 意为“低这一段颈”，1979 年那位护士把病房里没有一位病患肯测量的一段颈做了一遍。
neck 意为“颈；脖子”，指那段颈本身而不是细细的体温计，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被测量。
neck 意为“颈；脖子”，指病房里每一段旁边的那一段，每一段旁边都有同一支细细的体温计。
neck 意为“颈；脖子”，指最远那格药柜的留给孩子们服的那一剂，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
neck 意为“颈、胆气”，指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这段胆气就是那件事的全部。
neck 意为“胆气”，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西而不是那段颈，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
neck 意为“颈；脖子”，指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一段，到 1984 年这一段成了护理记录里的一行。
neck 意为“颈之事”，护士四月写道，整件事的颈之事是一处病房和三个夜晚的测量。
neck 意为“颈；脖子”，我记得的是护理记录里测量过的那一段，1986 年挺过了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一段。
neck 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，颈是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的颈。
